title: PIM Activator: install the extension on a machine without Intune
purpose: Installs the PIM Activator browser extension on this machine (Edge, Chrome or both) through local Chromium enterprise policy in the registry -- force-install, install source, extension settings and the tenant catalog -- for servers and machines without Intune; -Uninstall removes only what it wrote.
whenToRun: On a server or a machine that is not managed by Intune, once (PIM Manager > Operations > PIM Activator > Servers shows the command with your tenant and app). Re-run to change the settings; -Uninstall to remove them.

runAs.name: Local Administrator (elevated PowerShell)
runAs.scope: this machine; only for -Scope Machine (HKLM, the default)
runAs.why: machine policy lives under HKLM. -Scope User (HKCU, the current user only) needs no elevation.

runAs.name: Delegated sign-in: Organization.Read.All, Application.Read.All (read only)
runAs.scope: Microsoft Graph, for the first-party app Microsoft Graph Command Line Tools
runAs.why: ONLY when neither -TenantId + -ClientId nor -CatalogJsonPath is given: the tenant and the PIM Activator app are looked up live. The command PIM Manager shows passes both, so it signs in to nothing.

changes.object: <HKLM or HKCU>\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge and \Google\Chrome \ExtensionInstallForcelist: one row '<extension id>;<update URL>' in the slot already holding our id, else the lowest free slot; other rows carrying our id are removed
changes.why: the browser installs and keeps the extension updated

changes.object: ...\ExtensionInstallSources: one row with the update host pattern (https://<host>/*)
changes.why: allows the install where a hardened baseline restricts install sources
changes.undo: -Uninstall (kept while another forcelist row still installs from that host)

changes.object: ...\ExtensionSettings: our entry (force_installed, runtime_allowed_hosts) merged into the organisation's dictionary -- their entries are kept
changes.why: an extension update can never be silently disabled as a permission expansion

changes.object: ...\ExtensionInstallAllowlist: one row with our id -- only with -WriteAllowlist
changes.why: for environments that block every extension ('*' blocklist)

changes.object: ...\3rdparty\extensions\<extension id>\policy\tenantCatalog (tenant name, tenant id, app client id, activation defaults; plus -AdditionalTenantsJson tenants)
changes.why: the extension's 'Use centrally deployed' setup reads it

changes.object: with -Uninstall: our forcelist / allowlist / install-source rows, our ExtensionSettings entry and the 3rdparty\extensions\<extension id> key -- nothing of the organisation's
changes.why: removes the PIM Activator from this machine (the browser uninstalls it on its next start)

parameters.name: Scope
parameters.help: Machine (HKLM, every user, needs elevation) or User (HKCU, the current user only).

parameters.name: Channel
parameters.help: Released, or Test (the separate TEST extension id and update manifest).

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: With -ClientId: the tenant catalog is written from these values (no sign-in).

parameters.name: ClientId
parameters.help: Application (client) id of the PIM Activator app registration. Without it the app is looked up by exact -AppDisplayName (sign-in).

parameters.name: TenantName
parameters.help: The tenant name the users see in the extension.

parameters.name: AdditionalTenantsJson
parameters.help: Optional: more tenants for the extension's tenant switcher (JSON array of name, tenantId, clientId).

parameters.name: DefaultJustification
parameters.help: The justification the extension pre-fills (overrides the catalog's).

parameters.name: DefaultDurationHours
parameters.help: The activation length the extension pre-fills, 1-24 hours (overrides the catalog's).

parameters.name: AutoActivateMaxGroups
parameters.help: Per-device cap on auto-activation: 0 = off, N = at most N groups, -1 = remove the cap.

parameters.name: CatalogJsonPath
parameters.help: A tenant catalog JSON file to write instead of -TenantId/-ClientId or the live lookup.

parameters.name: SkipTenantCatalog
parameters.help: Write only the install policies, no tenant catalog.

parameters.name: WriteAllowlist
parameters.help: Also write ExtensionInstallAllowlist (only where every extension is blocked).

parameters.name: AppDisplayName
parameters.help: Exact display name used to find the app when -ClientId is not given (must be unique).

parameters.name: ExtensionId
parameters.help: The extension id; change it only for a fork.

parameters.name: UpdateUrl
parameters.help: The update manifest the browser installs and updates the extension from (self-hosting).

parameters.name: Uninstall
parameters.help: Remove only what this script wrote for the extension id.

readsOnly: this machine's current Edge / Chrome extension policies (so the organisation's own rows and settings are kept)
only without -TenantId + -ClientId: the tenant (organization) and the PIM Activator app registration, by exact name or -ClientId
network: none when -TenantId and -ClientId are given (the command PIM Manager shows)
login.microsoftonline.com, graph.microsoft.com -- only for the live lookup

knudsenmorten.github.io -- by the BROWSER afterwards, not by this script: the update manifest and the signed extension package (Chromium installs a package only when its signing key matches the extension id)
whatIf: Reads this machine's policies and prints every registry value it would set or remove (forcelist slot, install source, ExtensionSettings entry, tenant catalog, per-device cap). Nothing is written. A preview of -Scope Machine runs without elevation.
undo: Deploy-PimActivatorClient.ps1 -Uninstall (same -Scope, -Browser and -Channel): removes only this script's rows, entries and keys; the browser removes the extension on its next start.
